mutations)**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nServer Actions (functions with &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use server\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;) are exposed as public endpoints, just like API routes. Always verify authentication and authorization **inside** each Server Action—do not rely solely on middleware, layout guards, or page-level checks, as Server Actions can be invoked directly.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNext.js documentation explicitly states: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Treat Server Actions with the same security considerations as public-facing API endpoints, and verify if the user is allowed to perform a mutation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Incorrect (no authentication check):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function deleteUser(userId: string) {\\\\\\\\n  // Anyone can call this! action):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nimport { verifySession } from '@/lib/auth'\\\\\\\\nimport { unauthorized } from '@/lib/errors'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function deleteUser(userId: string) {\\\\\\\\n  // Always check auth inside the action\\\\\\\\n  const session = await verifySession()\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  if (!session) {\\\\\\\\n    throw unauthorized('Must be logged in')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Check authorization too\\\\\\\\n  if (session.user.role !== 'admin' \u0026\u0026 session.user.id !== userId) {\\\\\\\\n    throw unauthorized('Cannot delete other users')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  await db.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } })\\\\\\\\n  return { success: true This prevents logging, analytics, and other side effects from blocking the response.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Incorrect (blocks response):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\\\\\\\\n  // Perform mutation\\\\\\\\n  await updateDatabase(request)\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Logging (non-blocking):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { after } from 'next/server'\\\\\\\\nimport { headers, cookies } from 'next/headers'\\\\\\\\nimport { logUserAction } from sent\\\\\\\\n  after(async () =\u003e {\\\\\\\\n    const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown'\\\\\\\\n    const sessionCookie = (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous'\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\n    logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent })\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), {\\\\\\\\n    status: 200,\\\\\\\\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe response is sent immediately while logging happens in the background.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Common use cases:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Analytics tracking\\\\\\\\n- Audit logging\\\\\\\\n- Sending notifications\\\\\\\\n- Cache invalidation\\\\\\\\n- Cleanup tasks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important notes:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;after()&#96; runs even if the response fails or redirects\\\\\\\\n- Works in Server Actions, Route Handlers, and Server Components\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference: What are some good libraries to use with Next.js?\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ * \u0026#96;next-auth\u0026#96; or \u0026#96;better-auth\u0026#96; for authentication\\\\\\\\n+ * \u0026#96;swr\u0026#96; or \u0026#96;react-query\u0026#96; for data fetching\\\\\\\\n+ * \u0026#96;axios\u0026#96; for HTTP requests\\\\\\\\n+ * \u0026#96;tailwindcss\u0026#96; for styling\\\\\\\\n+ * \u0026#96;zod\u0026#96; for validation\\\\\\\\n+ * \u0026#96;drizzle-orm\u0026#96; or \u0026#96;prisma\u0026#96; for database\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ ## 81. Why choose Next.js for your next project?\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ * SEO-friendly with SSR/SSG\\\\\\\\n+ * Fast performance with automatic optimizations\\\\\\\\n+ * Great developer experience\\\\\\\\n+ * React Compiler for automatic optimization (Next.js 16+)\\\\\\\\n+ * Turbopack for faster builds (Next.js 16+)\\\\\\\\n+ * Strong community and ecosystem\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ ## 82. What are Server Actions in Next.js?\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ **New in Next.js 13+:** Server Actions allow you to run server-side code directly from Client Components. They use the \u0026#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use server\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u0026#96; directive and can be called from forms or event handlers.\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ ## 83. How do you use Server Actions in Next.js?\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ **New in Next.js 13+:** Define a Server Action with \u0026#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use server\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u0026#96;:\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ \u0026#96;\u0026#96;\u0026#96;ts\\\\\\\\n+ 'use server'\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\n+   const title = formData.get('title')\\\\\\\\n+   // Server-side logic\\\\\\\\n+ }\\\\\\\\n+ \u0026#96;\u0026#96;\u0026#96;\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ ## 84. What is the difference between Server Actions and API Routes?\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ Server Actions are simpler for form submissions and mutations, while API Routes are better for RESTful APIs and external integrations. Server Actions are type-safe and integrate better with forms.\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ ## 85. How do you handle errors in Next.js App Router?\\\\\\\\n+ \\\\\\\\n+ Use \u0026#96;error.tsx\u0026#96; files to create error boundaries. How to create forms with Server Actions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How it works\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact extends the HTML [&#96;\u003cform\u003e&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [&#96;action&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen used in a form, the function automatically receives the [&#96;FormData&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [&#96;FormData&#96; methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return \u003cform action={createInvoice}\u003e...\u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return \u003cform action={createInvoice}\u003e...\u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [&#96;Object.fromEntries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: &#96;const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)&#96;. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with &#96;$ACTION_&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Passing additional arguments\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOutside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [&#96;bind&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. For example, to pass the &#96;userId&#96; argument to the &#96;updateUser&#96; Server Function:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/client-component.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { updateUser } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function UserProfile({ userId }: { userId: string }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const updateUserWithId = updateUser.bind(null, userId)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={updateUserWithId}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cinput type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"name\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cbutton type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003eUpdate User Name\u003c/button\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n formData) {}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know**:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * An alternative is to pass arguments as hidden input fields in the form (e.g. &#96;\u003cinput type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"hidden\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"userId\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" value={userId} /\u003e&#96;). However, the value will be part of the rendered HTML and will not be encoded.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * &#96;bind&#96; works in both Server and Client Components and supports progressive enhancement.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Form validation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nForms can be validated on the client or server.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **client-side validation**, you can use the HTML attributes like &#96;required&#96; and &#96;type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"email\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; for basic validation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **server-side validation**, you can use a library like [zod](https://zod.dev/) to validate the form fields. For example:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/actions.ts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { z } from 'zod'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nconst schema = z.object({\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  email: z.string({\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    invalid_type_error: 'Invalid Email',\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default async function createUser(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const validatedFields = schema.safeParse({\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    email: formData.get('email'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  // Return early if the form data is invalid\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  if (!validatedFields.success) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    return {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      errors: validatedFields.error.flatten().fieldErrors,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  // Mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx }),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default async function createsUser(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const validatedFields = schema.safeParse({\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    email: a new &#96;prevState&#96; or &#96;initialState&#96; parameter as its first argument.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx initialState)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={formAction}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cbutton disabled={pending}\u003eSign up\u003c/button\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAlternatively, you can use the [&#96;useFormStatus&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/hooks/useFormStatus) hook to show a loading indicator while the action is being executed. When using this hook, you'll need to create a separate component to render the loading indicator. For example, to disable the button when the action is pending:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cbutton disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/button\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cbutton disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/button\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can then nest the &#96;SubmitButton&#96; component inside the form:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={createUser}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cSubmitButton /\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={createUser}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cSubmitButton /\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know:** In React 19, &#96;useFormStatus&#96; includes additional keys on the returned object, like data, method, and action. If you are not using React 19, only the &#96;pending&#96; key is available.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Optimistic updates\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can use the React [&#96;useOptimistic&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic) hook to optimistically update the UI before the Server Function finishes executing, rather than waiting for the response:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ntype Message = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  message: string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }: { messages: Message[] }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic\u003c\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    Message[],\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  \u003e(messages, (state, newMessage) =\u003e [...state, { message: newMessage }])\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData: FormData) =\u003e {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message') as string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m, i) =\u003e (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        \u003cdiv key={i}\u003e{m.message}\u003c/div\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cform action={formAction}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        \u003cinput type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" formData.get('message')\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Nested form elements\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can call Server Actions in elements nested inside &#96;\u003cform\u003e&#96; such as &#96;\u003cbutton\u003e&#96;, &#96;\u003cinput type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003e&#96;, and &#96;\u003cinput type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"image\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003e&#96;. These elements accept the &#96;formAction&#96; prop or event handlers.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis is useful in cases where you want to call multiple Server Actions within a form. For example, you can create a specific &#96;\u003cbutton\u003e&#96; element for saving a post draft in addition to publishing it. See the [React &#96;\u003cform\u003e&#96; docs](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/form#handling-multiple-submission-types) for more information.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Programmatic form submission\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can trigger a form submission programmatically using the [&#96;requestSubmit()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLFormElement/requestSubmit) method. For example, when the user submits a form using the &#96;⌘&#96; + &#96;Enter&#96; keyboard shortcut, you can listen for the &#96;onKeyDown&#96; event:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/entry.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey) \u0026\u0026\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === 'NumpadEnter')\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    ) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      e.preventDefault()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      e.currentTarget.form?.requestSubmit()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n How to create forms with Server Actions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How it works\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact extends the HTML [&#96;\u003cform\u003e&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [&#96;action&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen used in a form, the function automatically receives the [&#96;FormData&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [&#96;FormData&#96; methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return \u003cform action={createInvoice}\u003e...\u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return \u003cform action={createInvoice}\u003e...\u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [&#96;Object.fromEntries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: &#96;const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)&#96;. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with &#96;$ACTION_&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Passing additional arguments\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOutside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [&#96;bind&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. For example, to pass the &#96;userId&#96; argument to the &#96;updateUser&#96; Server Function:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx userId)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={updateUserWithId}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cinput However, the value will be part of the rendered HTML and will not be encoded.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e * &#96;bind&#96; works in both Server and Client Components and supports progressive enhancement.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Form validation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nForms can be validated on the client or server.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **client-side validation**, you can use the HTML attributes like &#96;required&#96; and &#96;type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"email\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; for basic validation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **server-side validation**, you can use a library like [zod](https://zod.dev/) to validate the form fields. )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAlternatively, you can use the [&#96;useFormStatus&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/hooks/useFormStatus) For example, to disable the button when the action is pending:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cbutton disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/button\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cbutton disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/button\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can then nest the &#96;SubmitButton&#96; component inside the form:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={createUser}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cSubmitButton /\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003cform action={createUser}\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      \u003cSubmitButton /\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/form\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\u003e **Good to know:** In React 19, &#96;useFormStatus&#96; includes additional keys on the returned object, like data, method, and action. If you are not using React 19, only the &#96;pending&#96; key is available.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Optimistic updates\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can use the React [&#96;useOptimistic&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic) hook to optimistically update the UI before the Server Function finishes executing, rather than waiting for the response:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ntype Message = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  message: string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }: { messages: Message[] }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast \u003e= AA.Technical constraints \u0026 stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout \u0026 sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta \u0026 SEO   - Proper &#96;\u003chead\u003e&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact \u0026 social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system \u0026 visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing \u0026 grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance \u0026 best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Only create the static visuals and seed data.- Do not include external analytics or tracking scripts.- Do not use non-free or proprietary fonts; prefer Google Fonts or system fallbacks.Tone for copywriting- Confident, concise, and human. Always start from the top and only move to the next source if the current one doesn't have the answer.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Priority | Source | What it contains |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| 1 | &#96;AGENTS.md&#96; (this file) | Project-specific conventions, templates, and decisions |\\\\\\\\n| 2 | Sub &#96;AGENTS-*.md&#96; files | Deep-dive guidelines (security, performance, accessibility, animations, testing) |\\\\\\\\n| 3 | Agent Skills (&#96;.agents/skills/&#96;) | Framework and tool knowledge (Next.js, Drizzle, better-auth, shadcn, etc.) |\\\\\\\\n| 4 | Indexed Docs (Cursor) | Official documentation indexed locally in Cursor |\\\\\\\\n| 5 | MCP Servers | Live browsing and external tool integrations |\\\\\\\\n| 6 | Web Search | Last resort — only when none of the above have the answer |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important**: Always prefer Cursor's indexed docs over web searches. Now I have a solid picture of your codebase. Let me give you a thorough answer.

---

## Are design patterns common in Next.js?

Yes, but with an important nuance: **Next.js itself already bakes in many design patterns** through its conventions. When you use the App Router, Server Components, Server Actions, route groups, and layouts — you're already applying patterns like:

- **Separation of Concerns** via `(admin)` / `(public)` route groups
- **Repository Pattern** (loosely) via your Drizzle queries in server actions
- **Command Pattern** via Server Actions (each action is a discrete command: `createProject`, `deleteSkill`, etc.)

So you're not starting from zero — your project already uses patterns implicitly.

## Which patterns from those links are relevant to your project?

Let me break this down from both the [Refactoring Guru catalog](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/catalog) and the [Dev.to article](https://dev.to/nithya_iyer/5-design-patterns-for-building-scalable-nextjs-applications-1c80), filtering for what **actually matters** for your specific portfolio + CMS project.

### Patterns you should NOT worry about

Most of the classic GoF patterns from Refactoring Guru (Singleton, Factory, Observer, etc.) are **object-oriented patterns designed for class-based architectures**. Your project uses functional React components, Server Components, and Server Actions — a very different paradigm. Applying them directly would add complexity without real benefit.

The Dev.to article is also somewhat outdated — it references `getStaticProps`, `getServerSideProps`, and the Pages Router, which don't apply to your App Router setup.

### Patterns that WOULD genuinely help your project

Based on what I found in your codebase, here are the patterns that would have **real, tangible impact**:

---

### 1. Container-Presentational Pattern (high value)

**What it is**: Separate data-fetching/logic from UI rendering.

**You're already partially doing this** — your dashboard pages (Server Components) fetch data and pass it to client components. But there's room to formalize it.

**Where it would help in your project**: Your admin pages like the projects list page fetch data and render UI in the same component. If you extract the table/list UI into a dedicated presentational component, you get:
- Reusable table components across entities (projects, experiences, skills)
- Easier testing (you can test the UI component with mock props)
- Cleaner page files that only handle data orchestration

**Example for your project**:

```typescript
// app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/page.tsx (Container - Server Component)
export default async function ProjectsPage() {
  const projects = await db.query.projects.findMany({ ... });
  return <ProjectsTable projects={projects} />;
}
```

```typescript
// components/admin/projects-table.tsx (Presentational - Client Component)
"use client";
export function ProjectsTable({ projects }: { projects: Project[] }) {
  // Only handles rendering, sorting UI, delete confirmation dialogs, etc.
}
```

---

### 2. Strategy Pattern — for Server Action validation (medium value)

**What it is**: Define a family of algorithms (strategies) and make them interchangeable.

**Why it fits**: Your server actions all follow the same 4-step pattern (authenticate, validate, execute, revalidate) but currently **skip authentication and validation**. A strategy-like approach would let you define reusable validation schemas per entity:

```typescript
// Each entity has its own Zod schema (strategy)
const projectSchema = z.object({ title: z.string().min(1), ... });
const skillSchema = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1), ... });

// The action "strategy" is: parse with the entity's schema, then execute
```

This isn't the formal Strategy pattern from the GoF book, but it's the same principle adapted to your functional architecture.

---

### 3. Facade Pattern — for data access (low-medium value)

**What it is**: Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.

**Where it fits**: Right now your dashboard pages query the database directly with Drizzle. If you create simple data-access functions in a `lib/queries/` folder, you centralize all DB logic:

```typescript
// lib/queries/projects.ts
export async function getProjectsWithSkills() {
  return db.query.projects.findMany({
    with: { projectSkills: { with: { skill: true } } },
    orderBy: [asc(projects.order)],
  });
}
```

Benefits: if you ever change how projects are fetched (add caching, change relations), you change it in one place instead of hunting through page files.

---

### 4. Error Boundary Pattern (high value, Next.js specific)

**What it is**: Catch and handle errors gracefully at component boundaries.

**Why it's critical for you**: Your project currently has **zero error handling** — no `error.tsx` files, no try-catch in server actions. If a database query fails, the entire page crashes with an unhandled error.

Next.js has built-in support for this via `error.tsx` files in route segments. This is essentially the Error Boundary pattern formalized by the framework.

---

## My recommendation

You don't need to adopt a bunch of patterns all at once. Here's what I'd prioritize, in order:

| Priority | Pattern | Why |
|----------|---------|-----|
| 1 | **Error Boundaries** (`error.tsx` files) | Your app has no error handling at all — this is a critical gap |
| 2 | **Server Action hardening** (auth + Zod validation) | Security risk — actions don't check sessions or validate input |
| 3 | **Container-Presentational** | Clean up your admin pages by separating data fetching from UI |
| 4 | **Facade for data access** (`lib/queries/`) | Centralize DB queries for reusability and maintainability |

Patterns 1 and 2 are less about "design patterns" in the academic sense and more about **essential production readiness**. Patterns 3 and 4 are the classical design pattern improvements that will help as your project grows.

---

## TL;DR

- You're already using patterns implicitly through Next.js conventions
- Most classic OOP patterns from Refactoring Guru don't map well to a functional React/Next.js project
- The most impactful improvements for **your specific project** are: error handling, input validation, and separating data concerns from UI concerns
- Don't over-engineer it — your project is a portfolio + CMS, not a massive SaaS. Apply patterns where they solve real problems, not for the sake of applying them

Would you like me to implement any of these patterns? I'd suggest starting with the error boundaries and server action hardening since those address actual bugs/security gaps.

Created the `AGENTS-PATTERNS.md` file and registered it in the main `AGENTS.md`. Here's what the document covers:

**1. Container-Presentational Pattern** — Split your 200+ line page files (like `projects/page.tsx`) into a thin container (data fetching + auth) and a presentational component (table UI, empty states). Also extracts duplicated formatting functions (`formatDate`, `getStatusVariant`) to `lib/utils.ts`.

**2. Server Action Hardening (Strategy-like)** — A 4-step template for every server action: authenticate with `getServerSession()`, validate with a Zod schema (one per entity in `lib/schemas/`), execute in a try-catch, then revalidate/redirect. Includes a status table showing all 5 action files need all 3 fixes, and a migration order for applying them.

**3. Data Access Facade** — Move inline Drizzle queries from page files into `lib/queries/` functions (e.g., `getProjectsWithSkills()`). Pages call these functions instead of `db` directly, making it trivial to add caching later in one place.

**4. Error Boundaries** — Add `error.tsx` files to catch runtime errors (DB failures, auth issues) with a user-friendly retry UI, plus `loading.tsx` files for skeleton loading states. Minimum 3 error boundaries: root, dashboard, and public.

The document also includes a **Pattern Interaction** section showing how all four patterns compose together in a typical request flow, a **Migration Flow** for the order to implement them, and a full **Implementation Checklist** with per-entity and global tasks.

Use when building Next.js applications, implementing SSR/SSG, or optimizing React Server Components.\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# Next.js App Router Patterns\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nComprehensive patterns for Next.js 14+ App Router architecture, Server Components, and modern full-stack React development.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## When to Use This Skill\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Building new Next.js applications with App Router\\\\\\\\n- Migrating from Pages Router to App Router\\\\\\\\n- Implementing Server Components and streaming\\\\\\\\n- Setting up parallel and intercepting routes\\\\\\\\n- Optimizing data fetching and caching\\\\\\\\n- Building full-stack features with Server Actions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Core Concepts\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 1. Rendering Modes\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Mode                  | Where        | When to Use                               |\\\\\\\\n| --------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |\\\\\\\\n| **Server Components** | Server only  | Data fetching, heavy computation, secrets |\\\\\\\\n| **Client Components** | Browser      | Interactivity, hooks, browser APIs        |\\\\\\\\n| **Static**            | Build time   | Content that rarely changes               |\\\\\\\\n| **Dynamic**           | Request time | Personalized or real-time data            |\\\\\\\\n| **Streaming**         | Progressive  | Large pages, slow data sources            |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### 2. File Conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── layout.tsx       # Shared UI wrapper\\\\\\\\n├── page.tsx         # Route UI\\\\\\\\n├── loading.tsx      # Loading UI (Suspense)\\\\\\\\n├── error.tsx        # Error boundary\\\\\\\\n├── not-found.tsx    # 404 UI\\\\\\\\n├── route.ts         # API endpoint\\\\\\\\n├── template.tsx     # Re-mounted layout\\\\\\\\n├── default.tsx      # Parallel route fallback\\\\\\\\n└── opengraph-image.tsx  # OG image generation\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Quick Start\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n// app/layout.tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { Inter } from 'next/font/google'\\\\\\\\nimport { Providers } from './providers'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nconst inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] })\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport const metadata = {\\\\\\\\n  title: { default: 'My App', template: '%s | My App' },\\\\\\\\n  description: 'Built with Next.js App Router',\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default function RootLayout({\\\\\\\\n  children,\\\\\\\\n}: {\\\\\\\\n  children: React.ReactNode\\\\\\\\n}) {\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\n    \u003chtml lang=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"en\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" suppressHydrationWarning\u003e\\\\\\\\n      \u003cbody className={inter.className}\u003e\\\\\\\\n        \u003cProviders\u003e{children}\u003c/Providers\u003e\\\\\\\\n      \u003c/body\u003e\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/html\u003e\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// app/page.tsx - Server Component by default\\\\\\\\nasync function getProducts() {\\\\\\\\n  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products', {\\\\\\\\n    next: { revalidate: 3600 }, // ISR: revalidate every hour\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n  return res.json()\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default async function HomePage() {\\\\\\\\n  const products = await getProducts()\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\n    \u003cmain\u003e\\\\\\\\n      \u003ch1\u003eProducts\u003c/h1\u003e\\\\\\\\n      \u003cProductGrid products={products} /\u003e\\\\\\\\n    \u003c/main\u003e\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Patterns\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Pattern 1: Server Components with Data Fetching\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n// app/products/page.tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { Suspense } from 'react'\\\\\\\\nimport { ProductList, ProductListSkeleton } from '@/components/products'\\\\\\\\nimport { FilterSidebar } from '@/components/filters'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\ninterface SearchParams {\\\\\\\\n  category?: string\\\\\\\\n  sort?: 'price' | 'name' | 'date'\\\\\\\\n  page?: string\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport default async function ProductsPage({\\\\\\\\n  searchParams,\\\\\\\\n}: {\\\\\\\\n  searchParams: Promise\u003cSearchParams\u003e\\\\\\\\n}) {\\\\\\\\n  const params = await &#96;layout.tsx&#96; | Shared UI for segment and children |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;loading.tsx&#96; | Loading UI (Suspense boundary) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;error.tsx&#96; | Error UI (Error boundary) |\\\\\\\\n| Metadata\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAdd SEO metadata to Next.js pages using the Metadata API.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Important: Server Components Only\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe &#96;metadata&#96; object and &#96;generateMetadata&#96; function are **only supported in Server Components**. They cannot be used in Client Components.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIf the target page has &#96;'use client'&#96;:\\\\\\\\n1. Remove &#96;'use client'&#96; if possible, move client logic to child components\\\\\\\\n2. Or extract metadata to a parent Server Component layout\\\\\\\\n3. Or split the file: Server Component with metadata imports Client Components\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Static Metadata\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport type { Metadata } from 'next'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport const metadata: Metadata = {\\\\\\\\n  title: 'Page Title',\\\\\\\\n  description: 'Page description for search engines',\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Dynamic Metadata\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport type { Metadata } from 'next'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\ntype Props = { params: Promise\u003c{ slug: string }\u003e }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function generateMetadata({ params }: Props): Promise\u003cMetadata\u003e {\\\\\\\\n  const { slug } = await params\\\\\\\\n  const post = await getPost(slug)\\\\\\\\n  return { title: post.title, description: post.description }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Avoid Duplicate Fetches\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUse React &#96;cache()&#96; when the same data is needed for both metadata and page:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { cache } from 'react'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport const getPost = cache(async (slug: string) =\u003e {\\\\\\\\n  return await db.posts.findFirst({ where: { slug } })\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Viewport\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSeparate from metadata for streaming support:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport type { Viewport } from 'next'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport const viewport: Viewport = {\\\\\\\\n  width: 'device-width',\\\\\\\\n  initialScale: 1,\\\\\\\\n  themeColor: '#000000',\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n// Or dynamic\\\\\\\\nexport function generateViewport({ params }): Viewport {\\\\\\\\n  return { themeColor: getThemeColor(params) }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Title Templates\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nIn root layout for consistent naming:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nexport const metadata: Metadata = {\\\\\\\\n  title: { default: 'Site Name', template: '%s | Site Name' },\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Metadata File Conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#metadata-file-conventions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPlace these files in &#96;app/&#96; directory (or route segments):\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| File | Purpose |\\\\\\\\n|------|---------|\\\\\\\\n| &#96;favicon.ico&#96; | Favicon |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;icon.png&#96; / &#96;icon.svg&#96; | App icon |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;apple-icon.png&#96; | Apple app icon |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;opengraph-image.png&#96; | OG image |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;twitter-image.png&#96; | Twitter card image |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;sitemap.ts&#96; / &#96;sitemap.xml&#96; | Sitemap (use &#96;generateSitemaps&#96; for multiple) |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;robots.ts&#96; / &#96;robots.txt&#96; | Robots directives |\\\\\\\\n| &#96;manifest.ts&#96; / &#96;manifest.json&#96; | Web app manifest |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## SEO Best Practice: Static Files Are Often Enough\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFor most sites, **static metadata files provide excellent SEO coverage**:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\napp/\\\\\\\\n├── favicon.ico\\\\\\\\n├── opengraph-image.png     # Works for both OG and Twitter\\\\\\\\n├── sitemap.ts\\\\\\\\n├── robots.ts\\\\\\\\n└── layout.tsx              # With title/description metadata\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Tips:**\\\\\\\\n- A single &#96;opengraph-image.png&#96; covers both Open Graph and Twitter (Twitter falls back to OG)\\\\\\\\n- Static &#96;title&#96; and &#96;description&#96; in layout metadata is sufficient for most pages\\\\\\\\n- Only use dynamic &#96;generateMetadata&#96; when content varies per page\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n# OG Image Generation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nGenerate dynamic Open Graph images using can't access search params, use route params instead\\\\\\\\n3. **Avoid Edge runtime** - Use default Node.js runtime\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\n// Good\\\\\\\\nimport { ImageResponse   "markdown": "# error.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nAn error file allows you to handle unexpected runtime errors and display fallback UI.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components\n\nimport { useEffect } from 'react'\n\nexport default function Error({\n  error,\n  reset,\n}: {\n  error: Error \u0026 { digest?: string }\n  reset: () =\u003e void\n}) {\n  useEffect(() =\u003e {\n    // Log the error to an error reporting service\n    console.error(error)\n  }, [error])\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eSomething went wrong!\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cbutton\n        onClick={\n          // Attempt to recover by trying to re-render the segment\n          () =\u003e reset()\n        }\n      \u003e\n        Try again\n      \u003c/button\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components\n\nimport { useEffect } from 'react'\n\nexport default function Error({ error, reset }) {\n  useEffect(() =\u003e {\n    // Log the error to an error reporting service\n    console.error(error)\n  }, [error])\n\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eSomething went wrong!\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cbutton\n        onClick={\n          // Attempt to recover by trying to re-render the segment\n          () =\u003e reset()\n        }\n      \u003e\n        Try again\n      \u003c/button\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;error.js&#96; wraps a route segment and its nested children in a [React Error Boundary](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary). When an error throws within the boundary, the &#96;error&#96; component shows as the fallback UI.\n\n\u003e - If you want errors to bubble up to the parent error boundary, you can &#96;throw&#96; when rendering the &#96;error&#96; component.\n\u003e - The [React DevTools](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) allow you to toggle error boundaries to test error states.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n## Reference\n\n### Props\n\n#### &#96;error&#96;\n\nAn instance of an [&#96;Error&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Error) object forwarded to the &#96;error.js&#96; Client Component.\n\n\u003e Good to know: During development, the &#96;Error&#96; object forwarded to the client will be serialized and include the &#96;message&#96; of the original error for easier debugging. However, this behavior is different in production to avoid leaking potentially sensitive details included in the error to the client.\n\n#### &#96;error.message&#96;\n\n- Errors forwarded from Server Components show a generic message with an identifier. This is to prevent leaking sensitive details. You can use the identifier, under &#96;errors.digest&#96;, to match the corresponding server-side logs.\n- Errors forwarded from Client Components show the original &#96;Error&#96; message.\n\n#### &#96;error.digest&#96;\n\nAn automatically generated hash of the error thrown. It can be used to match the corresponding error in server-side logs.\n\n#### &#96;reset&#96;\n\nThe cause of an error can sometimes be temporary. In these cases, trying again might resolve the issue.\n\nAn error component can use the &#96;reset()&#96; function to prompt the user to attempt to recover from the error. When executed, the function will try to re-render the error boundary's contents. If successful, the fallback error component is replaced with the result of the re-render.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components\n\nexport default function Error({\n  error,\n  reset,\n}: {\n  error: Error \u0026 { digest?: string }\n  reset: () =\u003e void\n}) {\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eSomething went wrong!\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cbutton onClick={() =\u003e reset()}\u003eTry again\u003c/button\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components\n\nexport default function Error({ error, reset }) {\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eSomething went wrong!\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cbutton onClick={() =\u003e reset()}\u003eTry again\u003c/button\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Examples\n\n### Global Error\n\nWhile less common, you can handle errors in the root layout or template using &#96;global-error.jsx&#96;, located in the root app directory, even when leveraging [internationalization](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/internationalization). Global error UI must define its own &#96;and&#96; tags, global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your error page requires. This file replaces the root layout or template when active.\n\n\u003e Good to know: Error boundaries must be [Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#using-client-components), which means that [&#96;metadata&#96; and &#96;generateMetadata&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) exports are not supported in &#96;global-error.jsx&#96;. As an alternative, you can use the React [&#96;&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/title) component.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components\n\nexport default function GlobalError({\n  error,\n  reset,\n}: {\n  error: Error \u0026 { digest?: string }\n  reset: () =\u003e void\n}) {\n  return (\n    // global-error must include html and body tags\n    \u003chtml\u003e\n      \u003cbody\u003e\n        \u003ch2\u003eSomething went wrong!\u003c/h2\u003e\n        \u003cbutton onClick={() =\u003e reset()}\u003eTry again\u003c/button\u003e\n      \u003c/body\u003e\n    \u003c/html\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components\n\nexport default function GlobalError({ error, reset }) {\n  return (\n    // global-error must include html and body tags\n    \u003chtml\u003e\n      \u003cbody\u003e\n        \u003ch2\u003eSomething went wrong!\u003c/h2\u003e\n        \u003cbutton onClick={() =\u003e reset()}\u003eTry again\u003c/button\u003e\n      \u003c/body\u003e\n    \u003c/html\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Graceful error recovery with a custom error boundary\n\nWhen rendering fails on the client, it can be useful to show the last known server rendered UI for a better user experience.\n\nThe &#96;GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary&#96; is an example of a custom error boundary that captures and preserves the current HTML before an error occurs. If a rendering error happens, it re-renders the captured HTML and displays a persistent notification bar to inform the user.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use client'\n\nimport React, { Component, ErrorInfo, ReactNode } from 'react'\n\ninterface ErrorBoundaryProps {\n  children: ReactNode\n  onError?: (error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) =\u003e void\n}\n\ninterface ErrorBoundaryState {\n  hasError: boolean\n}\n\nexport class GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary extends Component\u003c\n  ErrorBoundaryProps,\n  ErrorBoundaryState\n\u003e {\n  private contentRef: React.RefObject\u003cHTMLDivElement | null\u003e\n\n  constructor(props: ErrorBoundaryProps) {\n    super(props)\n    this.state = { hasError: false }\n    this.contentRef = React.createRef()\n  }\n\n  static getDerivedStateFromError(_: Error): ErrorBoundaryState {\n    return { hasError: true }\n  }\n\n  componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) {\n    if (this.props.onError) {\n      this.props.onError(error, errorInfo)\n    }\n  }\n\n  render() {\n    if (this.state.hasError) {\n      // Render the current HTML content without hydration\n      return (\n        \u003c\u003e\n      }}\n          /\u003e\n          \u003cdiv className=\"fixed bottom-0 left-0 right-0 bg-red-600 text-white py-4 px-6 text-center\"\u003e\n            \u003cp className=\"font-semibold\"\u003e\n              An error occurred during page rendering\n            \u003c/p\u003e\n          \u003c/div\u003e\n        \u003c/\u003e\n      )\n    }\n\n    return \u003cdiv ref={this.contentRef}\u003e{this.props.children}\u003c/div\u003e\n  }\n}\n\nexport default GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n'use client'\n\nimport React, { ref={this.contentRef}\u003e{this.props.children}\u003c/div\u003e\n  }\n}\n\nexport default GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | Changes |\n| --- | {
  "markdown": "# loading.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nThe special file &#96;loading.js&#96; helps you create meaningful Loading UI with [React Suspense](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). With this convention, you can show an [instant loading state](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) from the server while the content of a route segment streams in. The new content is automatically swapped in once complete.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport default function Loading() {\n  // Or a custom loading skeleton component\n  return \u003cp\u003eLoading...\u003c/p\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nexport default function Loading() {\n  // Or a custom loading skeleton component\n  return \u003cp\u003eLoading...\u003c/p\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nInside the &#96;loading.js&#96; file, you can add any light-weight loading UI. You may find it helpful to use the [React Developer Tools](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) to manually toggle Suspense boundaries.\n\nBy default, this file is a [Server Component](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) - but can also be used as a Client Component through the &#96;\"use client\"&#96; directive.\n\n## Reference\n\n### Parameters\n\nLoading UI components do not accept any parameters.\n\n## Behavior\n\n### Navigation\n\n- Shared layouts remain interactive while new route segments load.\n- Navigation is interruptible, meaning changing routes does not need to wait for the content of the route to fully load before navigating to another route.\n- The Fallback UI is [prefetched](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching), making navigation immediate unless prefetching hasn't completed.\n\n### Instant Loading States\n\nAn instant loading state is fallback UI that is shown immediately upon navigation. You can pre-render loading indicators such as skeletons and spinners, or a small but meaningful part of future screens such as a cover photo, title, etc. This helps users understand the app is responding and provides a better user experience.\n\nCreate a loading state by adding a &#96;loading.js&#96; file inside a folder.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport default function Loading() {\n  // You can add any UI inside Loading, including a Skeleton.\n  return \u003cLoadingSkeleton /\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nexport default function Loading() {\n  // You can add any UI inside Loading, including a Skeleton.\n  return \u003cLoadingSkeleton /\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn the same folder, &#96;loading.js&#96; will be nested inside &#96;layout.js&#96;. It will automatically wrap the &#96;page.js&#96; file and any children below in a &#96;&#96; boundary.\n\n### SEO\n\n- Since streaming is server-rendered, it does not impact SEO. You can use the [Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) tool from Google to see how your page appears to Google's web crawlers and view the serialized HTML ([source](https://web.dev/rendering-on-the-web/#seo-considerations)).\n- Otherwise, [streaming metadata](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) may be used. Next.js automatically detects user agents to choose between blocking and streaming behavior.\n- For bots that only scrape static HTML, and cannot execute JavaScript like a full browser, such as Twitterbot, Next.js resolves [&#96;generateMetadata&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) before streaming UI, and metadata is placed in the &#96;&#96; of the initial HTML.\n\n### Status Codes\n\nWhen streaming, a &#96;200&#96; status code will be returned to signal that the request was successful.\n\nThe server can still communicate errors or issues to the client within the streamed content itself, for example, when using [&#96;redirect&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) or [&#96;notFound&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found). Because the response headers have already been sent to the client, the status code of the response cannot be updated.\n\nFor example, when a 404 page is streamed to the client, Next.js includes a &#96;&#96; tag in the streamed HTML. This prevents search engines from indexing that URL even if the HTTP status is 200. See Google’s guidance on the [&#96;robots&#96; meta tag](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).\n\nSome crawlers may label these responses as “soft 404s”. In the streaming case, this does not lead to indexation because the page is explicitly marked &#96;noindex&#96; in the HTML.\n\nIf you need a 404 status, for compliance or analytics, ensure the resource exists before the response body is streamed, so that the server can set the HTTP status code.\n\nYou can run this check in [&#96;proxy&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) to rewrite missing slugs to a not-found route, or [produce a 404 response](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#producing-a-response). Keep proxy checks fast, and avoid fetching full content there.\n\nWhen is the response body streamed?\n\nThe response body starts streaming when a Suspense fallback renders (for example, a &#96;loading.tsx&#96;) or when a Server Component suspends under a &#96;Suspense&#96; boundary. Place &#96;notFound()&#96; before those boundaries and before any &#96;await&#96; that may suspend.\n\nTo start streaming, the response headers must be set. This is why it is not possible to change the status code after streaming started.\n\n### Browser limits\n\n[Some browsers](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=252413) buffer a streaming response. You may not see the streamed response until the response exceeds 1024 bytes. This typically only affects “hello world” applications, but not real applications.\n\n## Platform Support\n\n| Deployment Option | Supported |\n| --- | --- |\n| [Node.js server](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#nodejs-server) | Yes |\n| [Docker container](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#docker) | Yes |\n| [Static export](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#static-export) | No |\n| [Adapters](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/deploying#adapters) | Platform-specific |\n\nLearn how to [configure streaming](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/self-hosting#streaming-and-suspense) when self-hosting Next.js.\n\n## Examples\n\n### Streaming with Suspense\n\nIn addition to &#96;loading.js&#96;, you can also manually create Suspense Boundaries for your own UI components. The App Router supports streaming with [Suspense](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense).\n\n&#96;&#96; works by wrapping a component that performs an asynchronous action (e.g. fetch data), showing fallback UI (e.g. skeleton, spinner) while it's happening, and then swapping in your component once the action completes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { Suspense } from 'react'\nimport { PostFeed, Weather } from './Components'\n\nexport default function Posts() {\n  return (\n    \u003csection\u003e\n      \u003cSuspense fallback={\u003cp\u003eLoading feed...\u003c/p\u003e}\u003e\n        \u003cPostFeed /\u003e\n      \u003c/Suspense\u003e\n      \u003cSuspense fallback={\u003cp\u003eLoading weather...\u003c/p\u003e}\u003e\n        \u003cWeather /\u003e\n      \u003c/Suspense\u003e\n    \u003c/section\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nimport { Suspense } from 'react'\nimport { PostFeed, Weather } from './Components'\n\nexport default function Posts() {\n  return (\n    \u003csection\u003e\n      \u003cSuspense fallback={\u003cp\u003eLoading feed...\u003c/p\u003e}\u003e\n        \u003cPostFeed /\u003e\n      \u003c/Suspense\u003e\n      \u003cSuspense fallback={\u003cp\u003eLoading weather...\u003c/p\u003e}\u003e\n        \u003cWeather /\u003e\n      \u003c/Suspense\u003e\n    \u003c/section\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy using Suspense, you get the benefits of:\n\n1. Selective Hydration - React prioritizes what components to make interactive first based on user interaction.\n2. Streaming Server Rendering - Progressively rendering HTML from the server to the client.\n\nFor more Suspense examples and use cases, please see the [React Documentation](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense).\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | Changes |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;v13.0.0&#96; | &#96;loading&#96; introduced. |\n\n---\n\nFor an overview of all available documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt)",

  "markdown": "# default.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nThe &#96;default.js&#96; file is used to render a fallback within [Parallel Routes](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) when Next.js cannot recover a [slot's](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes#slots) active state after a full-page load.\n\nDuring [soft navigation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions), Next.js keeps track of the active state (subpage) for each slot. However, for hard navigations (full-page load), Next.js cannot recover the active state. In this case, a &#96;default.js&#96; file can be rendered for subpages that don't match the current URL.\n\nConsider the following folder structure. The &#96;@team&#96; slot has a &#96;settings&#96; page, but &#96;@analytics&#96; does not.\n\nWhen navigating to &#96;/settings&#96;, the &#96;@team&#96; slot will render the &#96;settings&#96; page while maintaining the currently active page for the &#96;@analytics&#96; slot.\n\nOn refresh, Next.js will render a &#96;default.js&#96; for &#96;@analytics&#96;. If &#96;default.js&#96; doesn't exist, an error is returned for named slots (&#96;@team&#96;, &#96;@analytics&#96;, etc) and requires you to define a &#96;default.js&#96; in order to continue. If you want to preserve the old behavior of returning a 404 in these situations, you can create a &#96;default.js&#96; that contains:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport { notFound } from 'next/navigation'\n\nexport default function Default() {\n  notFound()\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAdditionally, since &#96;children&#96; is an implicit slot, you also need to create a &#96;default.js&#96; file to render a fallback for &#96;children&#96; when Next.js cannot recover the active state of the parent page. If you don't create a &#96;default.js&#96; for the &#96;children&#96; slot, it will return a 404 page for the route.\n\n## Reference\n\n### &#96;params&#96; (optional)\n\nA promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) from the root segment down to the slot's subpages. For example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport default async function Default({\n  params,\n}: {\n  params: Promise\u003c{ artist: string }\u003e\n}) {\n  const { artist } = await params\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nexport default async function Default({ params }) {\n  const { artist } = await params\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n| Example | URL | &#96;params&#96; |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;app/[artist]/@sidebar/default.js&#96; | &#96;/zack&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ artist: 'zack' }\u003e&#96; |\n| &#96;app/[artist]/[album]/@sidebar/default.js&#96; | &#96;/zack/next&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ artist: 'zack', album: 'next' }\u003e&#96; |\n\n- In version 14 and earlier, &#96;params&#96; was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.\n- Since the &#96;params&#96; prop is a promise. You must use &#96;async/await&#96; or React's [&#96;use&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.\n\n## Learn more about Parallel Routes- [Parallel Routes](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes)\n\n- Simultaneously render one or more pages in the same view that can be navigated independently. A pattern for highly dynamic applications.\n\n---\n\nFor an overview of all available documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt)",
