  "markdown": "# not-found.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nNext.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:\n\n- &#96;global-not-found.js&#96;: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.\n- &#96;not-found.js&#96;: Used when you call the [&#96;notFound&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.\n\n## &#96;not-found.js&#96;\n\nThe not-found file is used to render UI when the [&#96;notFound&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a &#96;200&#96; HTTP status code for streamed responses, and &#96;404&#96; for non-streamed responses.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport Link from 'next/link'\n\nexport default function NotFound() {\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eNot Found\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eCould not find requested resource\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003cLink href=\"/\"\u003eReturn Home\u003c/Link\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nimport Link from 'next/link'\n\nexport default function NotFound() {\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eNot Found\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eCould not find requested resource\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003cLink href=\"/\"\u003eReturn Home\u003c/Link\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## &#96;global-not-found.js&#96; (experimental)\n\nThe &#96;global-not-found.js&#96; file lets you define a 404 page for your entire application. Unlike &#96;not-found.js&#96;, which works at the route level, this is used when a requested URL doesn't match any route at all. Next.js skips rendering and directly returns this global page.\n\nThe &#96;global-not-found.js&#96; file bypasses your app's normal rendering, which means you'll need to import any global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your 404 page requires.\n\n\u003e Good to know: A smaller version of your global styles, and a simpler font family could improve performance of this page.\n\n&#96;global-not-found.js&#96; is useful when you can't build a 404 page using a combination of &#96;layout.js&#96; and &#96;not-found.js&#96;. This can happen in two cases:\n\n- Your root layout is defined using top-level dynamic segments (e.g. &#96;app/[country]/layout.tsx&#96;), which makes composing a consistent 404 page harder.\n- Your app has multiple root layouts (e.g. &#96;app/(admin)/layout.tsx&#96; and &#96;app/(shop)/layout.tsx&#96;), so there's no single layout to compose a global 404 from.\n\nTo enable it, add the &#96;globalNotFound&#96; flag in &#96;next.config.ts&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport type { NextConfig } from 'next'\n\nconst nextConfig: NextConfig = {\n  experimental: {\n    globalNotFound: true,\n  },\n}\n\nexport default nextConfig\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThen, create a file in the root of the &#96;app&#96; directory: &#96;app/global-not-found.js&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n// Import global styles and fonts\nimport './globals.css'\nimport { Inter } from 'next/font/google'\nimport type { Metadata } from 'next'\n\nconst inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] })\n\nexport const metadata: Metadata = {\n  title: '404 - Page Not Found',\n  description: 'The page you are looking for does not exist.',\n}\n\nexport default function GlobalNotFound() {\n  return (\n    \u003chtml lang=\"en\" className={inter.className}\u003e\n      \u003cbody\u003e\n        \u003ch1\u003e404 - Page Not Found\u003c/h1\u003e\n        \u003cp\u003eThis page does not exist.\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003c/body\u003e\n    \u003c/html\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n// Import global styles and fonts\nimport './globals.css'\nimport { Inter } from 'next/font/google'\n\nconst inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'] })\n\nexport const metadata = {\n  title: '404 - Page Not Found',\n  description: 'The page you are looking for does not exist.',\n}\n\nexport default function GlobalNotFound() {\n  return (\n    \u003chtml lang=\"en\" className={inter.className}\u003e\n      \u003cbody\u003e\n        \u003ch1\u003e404 - Page Not Found\u003c/h1\u003e\n        \u003cp\u003eThis page does not exist.\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003c/body\u003e\n    \u003c/html\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUnlike &#96;not-found.js&#96;, this file must return a full HTML document, including &#96;and&#96; tags.\n\n## Reference\n\n### Props\n\n&#96;not-found.js&#96; or &#96;global-not-found.js&#96; components do not accept any props.\n\n\u003e Good to know: In addition to catching expected &#96;notFound()&#96; errors, the root &#96;app/not-found.js&#96; and &#96;app/global-not-found.js&#96; files handle any unmatched URLs for your whole application. This means users that visit a URL that is not handled by your app will be shown the exported UI.\n\n## Examples\n\n### Data Fetching\n\nBy default, &#96;not-found&#96; is a Server Component. You can mark it as &#96;async&#96; to fetch and display data:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport Link from 'next/link'\nimport { headers } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport default async function NotFound() {\n  const headersList = await headers()\n  const domain = headersList.get('host')\n  const data = await getSiteData(domain)\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eNot Found: {data.name}\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eCould not find requested resource\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003e\n        View \u003cLink href=\"/blog\"\u003eall posts\u003c/Link\u003e\n      \u003c/p\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nimport Link from 'next/link'\nimport { headers } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport default async function NotFound() {\n  const headersList = await headers()\n  const domain = headersList.get('host')\n  const data = await getSiteData(domain)\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      \u003ch2\u003eNot Found: {data.name}\u003c/h2\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eCould not find requested resource\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003e\n        View \u003cLink href=\"/blog\"\u003eall posts\u003c/Link\u003e\n      \u003c/p\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf you need to use Client Component hooks like &#96;usePathname&#96; to display content based on the path, you must fetch data on the client-side instead.\n\n### Metadata\n\nFor &#96;global-not-found.js&#96;, you can export a &#96;metadata&#96; object or a [&#96;generateMetadata&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata) function to customize the &#96;&#96;, &#96; &#96;, and other head tags for your 404 page:\n\n\u003e Good to know: Next.js automatically injects &#96; &#96; for pages that return a 404 status code, including &#96;global-not-found.js&#96; pages.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nimport type { Metadata } from 'next'\n\nexport const metadata: Metadata = {\n  title: 'Not Found',\n  description: 'The page you are looking for does not exist.',\n}\n\nexport default function GlobalNotFound() {\n  return (\n    \u003chtml lang=\"en\"\u003e\n      \u003cbody\u003e\n        \u003cdiv\u003e\n          \u003ch1\u003eNot Found\u003c/h1\u003e\n          \u003cp\u003eThe page you are looking for does not exist.\u003c/p\u003e\n        \u003c/div\u003e\n      \u003c/body\u003e\n    \u003c/html\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nexport const metadata = {\n  title: 'Not Found',\n  description: 'The page you are looking for does not exist.',\n}\n\nexport default function GlobalNotFound() {\n  return (\n    \u003chtml lang=\"en\"\u003e\n      \u003cbody\u003e\n        \u003cdiv\u003e\n          \u003ch1\u003eNot Found\u003c/h1\u003e\n          \u003cp\u003eThe page you are looking for does not exist.\u003c/p\u003e\n        \u003c/div\u003e\n      \u003c/body\u003e\n    \u003c/html\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | Changes |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;v15.4.0&#96; | &#96;global-not-found.js&#96; introduced (experimental). |\n| &#96;v13.3.0&#96; | Root &#96;app/not-found&#96; handles global unmatched URLs. |\n| &#96;v13.0.0&#96; | &#96;not-found&#96; introduced. |\n\n---\n\nFor an overview of all available documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt)",

{
  "markdown": "# template.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nA template file is similar to a [layout](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages#creating-a-layout) in that it wraps a layout or page. Unlike layouts that persist across routes and maintain state, templates are given a unique key, meaning children Client Components reset their state on navigation.\n\nThey are useful when you need to:\n\n- To change default framework behavior. For example, Suspense boundaries inside layouts only show a fallback on first load, while templates show it on every navigation.\n- Reset the state of a child Client Components on navigation. For example, an input field.\n- Resynchronize &#96;useEffect&#96; on navigation.\n\n## Convention\n\nA template can be defined by exporting a default React component from a &#96;template.js&#96; file. The component should accept a &#96;children&#96; prop.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nexport default function Template({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {\n  return \u003cdiv\u003e{children}\u003c/div\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\nexport default function Template({ children }) {\n  return \u003cdiv\u003e{children}\u003c/div\u003e\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn terms of nesting, &#96;template.js&#96; is rendered between a layout and its children. Here's a simplified output:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cLayout\u003e\n  {/* Note that the template is given a unique key. */}\n  \u003cTemplate key={routeParam}\u003e{children}\u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/Layout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Props\n\n### &#96;children&#96; (required)\n\nTemplate accepts a &#96;children&#96; prop.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cLayout\u003e\n  {/* Note that the template is automatically given a unique key. */}\n  \u003cTemplate key={routeParam}\u003e{children}\u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/Layout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Behavior\n\n- DOM reset: DOM elements inside the template are fully recreated.\n- Effect re-run: Effects like &#96;useEffect&#96; will re-synchronize as the component remounts.\n- State reset: Any Client Component inside the template will reset its state on navigation.\n- With navigation: Templates receive a unique key for their own segment level. They remount when that segment (including its dynamic params) changes. Navigations within deeper segments do not remount higher-level templates. Search params do not trigger remounts.\n- Server Components: By default, templates are Server Components.\n\n### Templates during navigation and remounting\n\nThis section illustrates how templates behave during navigation. It shows, step by step, which templates remount on each route change and why.\n\nUsing this project tree:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\napp\n├── about\n│   ├── page.tsx\n├── blog\n│   ├── [slug]\n│   │   └── page.tsx\n│   ├── page.tsx\n│   └── template.tsx\n├── layout.tsx\n├── page.tsx\n└── template.tsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nStarting at &#96;/&#96;, the React tree looks roughly like this.\n\n\u003e Note: The &#96;key&#96; values shown in the examples are illustrative, the values in your application may differ.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cRootLayout\u003e\n  {/* app/template.tsx */}\n  \u003cTemplate key=\"/\"\u003e\n    \u003cPage /\u003e\n  \u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/RootLayout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNavigating to &#96;/about&#96; (first segment changes), the root template key changes, it remounts:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cRootLayout\u003e\n  {/* app/template.tsx */}\n  \u003cTemplate key=\"/about\"\u003e\n    \u003cAboutPage /\u003e\n  \u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/RootLayout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNavigating to &#96;/blog&#96; (first segment changes), the root template key changes, it remounts and the blog-level template mounts:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cRootLayout\u003e\n  {/* app/template.tsx (root) */}\n  \u003cTemplate key=\"/blog\"\u003e\n    {/* app/blog/template.tsx */}\n    \u003cTemplate key=\"/blog\"\u003e\n      \u003cBlogIndexPage /\u003e\n    \u003c/Template\u003e\n  \u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/RootLayout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNavigating within the same first segment to &#96;/blog/first-post&#96; (child segment changes), the root template key doesn't change, but the blog-level template key changes, it remounts:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cRootLayout\u003e\n  {/* app/template.tsx (root) */}\n  \u003cTemplate key=\"/blog\"\u003e\n    {/* app/blog/template.tsx */}\n    {/* remounts because the child segment at this level changed */}\n    \u003cTemplate key=\"/blog/first-post\"\u003e\n      \u003cBlogPostPage slug=\"first-post\" /\u003e\n    \u003c/Template\u003e\n  \u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/RootLayout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNavigating to &#96;/blog/second-post&#96; (same first segment, different child segment), the root template key doesn't change, but the blog-level template key changes, it remounts again:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n\u003cRootLayout\u003e\n  {/* app/template.tsx (root) */}\n  \u003cTemplate key=\"/blog\"\u003e\n    {/* app/blog/template.tsx */}\n    {/* remounts again due to changed child segment */}\n    \u003cTemplate key=\"/blog/second-post\"\u003e\n      \u003cBlogPostPage slug=\"second-post\" /\u003e\n    \u003c/Template\u003e\n  \u003c/Template\u003e\n\u003c/RootLayout\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | Changes |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;v13.0.0&#96; | &#96;template&#96; introduced. |\n\n---\n\nFor an overview of all available documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt)",

}

  "markdown": "# route.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nRoute Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function GET() {\n  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET() {\n  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Reference\n\n### HTTP Methods\n\nA route file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: &#96;GET&#96;, &#96;POST&#96;, &#96;PUT&#96;, &#96;PATCH&#96;, &#96;DELETE&#96;, &#96;HEAD&#96;, and &#96;OPTIONS&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {}\n\nexport async function HEAD(request: Request) {}\n\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {}\n\nexport async function PUT(request: Request) {}\n\nexport async function DELETE(request: Request) {}\n\nexport async function PATCH(request: Request) {}\n\n// If &#96;OPTIONS&#96; is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement &#96;OPTIONS&#96; and set the appropriate Response &#96;Allow&#96; header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.\nexport async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request) {}\n\nexport async function HEAD(request) {}\n\nexport async function POST(request) {}\n\nexport async function PUT(request) {}\n\nexport async function DELETE(request) {}\n\nexport async function PATCH(request) {}\n\n// If &#96;OPTIONS&#96; is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement &#96;OPTIONS&#96; and set the appropriate Response &#96;Allow&#96; header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.\nexport async function OPTIONS(request) {}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\n#### &#96;request&#96; (optional)\n\nThe &#96;request&#96; object is a [NextRequest](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. &#96;NextRequest&#96; gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing &#96;cookies&#96; and an extended, parsed, URL object &#96;nextUrl&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const url = request.nextUrl\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const url = request.nextUrl\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### &#96;context&#96; (optional)\n\n- &#96;params&#96;: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function GET(\n  request: Request,\n  { params }: { params: Promise\u003c{ team: string }\u003e }\n) {\n  const { team } = await params\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request, { params }) {\n  const { team } = await params\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n| Example | URL | &#96;params&#96; |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;app/dashboard/[team]/route.js&#96; | &#96;/dashboard/1&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ team: '1' }\u003e&#96; |\n| &#96;app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js&#96; | &#96;/shop/1/2&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ tag: '1', item: '2' }\u003e&#96; |\n| &#96;app/blog/[...slug]/route.js&#96; | &#96;/blog/1/2&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ slug: ['1', '2'] }\u003e&#96; |\n\n### Route Context Helper\n\nYou can type the Route Handler context using &#96;RouteContext&#96; to get strongly typed &#96;params&#96; from a route literal. &#96;RouteContext&#96; is a globally available helper.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'\n\nexport async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext\u003c'/users/[id]'\u003e) {\n  const { id } = await ctx.params\n  return Response.json({ id })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e - After type generation, the &#96;RouteContext&#96; helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.\n\u003e - Types are generated during &#96;next dev&#96;, &#96;next build&#96; or &#96;next typegen&#96;.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know\n\n## Examples\n\n### Cookies\n\nYou can read or set cookies with [&#96;cookies&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) from &#96;next/headers&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\n\n  const a = cookieStore.get('a')\n  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')\n  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\n\n  const a = cookieStore.get('a')\n  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')\n  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAlternatively, you can return a new &#96;Response&#96; using the [&#96;Set-Cookie&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\n  const token = cookieStore.get('token')\n\n  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: { 'Set-Cookie': &#96;token=${token.value}&#96; },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\n  const token = cookieStore.get('token')\n\n  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: { 'Set-Cookie': &#96;token=${token.value}&#96; },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can also use the underlying Web APIs to read cookies from the request ([&#96;NextRequest&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request)):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { type NextRequest } from 'next/server'\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const token = request.cookies.get('token')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const token = request.cookies.get('token')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Headers\n\nYou can read headers with [&#96;headers&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) from &#96;next/headers&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { headers } from 'next/headers'\nimport type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const headersList = await headers()\n  const referer = headersList.get('referer')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { headers } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const headersList = await headers()\n  const referer = headersList.get('referer')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis &#96;headers&#96; instance is read-only. To set headers, you need to return a new &#96;Response&#96; with new &#96;headers&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { headers } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const headersList = await headers()\n  const referer = headersList.get('referer')\n\n  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: { referer: referer },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { headers } from 'next/headers'\n\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const headersList = await headers()\n  const referer = headersList.get('referer')\n\n  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: { referer: referer },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can also use the underlying Web APIs to read headers from the request ([&#96;NextRequest&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request)):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { type NextRequest } from 'next/server'\n\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  const requestHeaders = new Headers(request.headers)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Revalidating Cached Data\n\nYou can [revalidate cached data](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration) using the &#96;revalidate&#96; route segment config option.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport const revalidate = 60\n\nexport async function GET() {\n  const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog')\n  const posts = await data.json()\n\n  return Response.json(posts)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport const revalidate = 60\n\nexport async function GET() {\n  const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog')\n  const posts = await data.json()\n\n  return Response.json(posts)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Redirects\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { redirect } from 'next/navigation'\n\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  redirect('https://nextjs.org/')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { redirect } from 'next/navigation'\n\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  redirect('https://nextjs.org/')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Dynamic Route Segments\n\nRoute Handlers can use [Dynamic Segments](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to create request handlers from dynamic data.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function GET(\n  request: Request,\n  { params }: { params: Promise\u003c{ slug: string }\u003e }\n) {\n  const { slug } = await params // 'a', 'b', or 'c'\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request, { params }) {\n  const { slug } = await params // 'a', 'b', or 'c'\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n| Route | Example URL | &#96;params&#96; |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;app/items/[slug]/route.js&#96; | &#96;/items/a&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ slug: 'a' }\u003e&#96; |\n| &#96;app/items/[slug]/route.js&#96; | &#96;/items/b&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ slug: 'b' }\u003e&#96; |\n| &#96;app/items/[slug]/route.js&#96; | &#96;/items/c&#96; | &#96;Promise\u003c{ slug: 'c' }\u003e&#96; |\n\n#### Static Generation with &#96;generateStaticParams&#96;\n\nYou can use [&#96;generateStaticParams&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) with dynamic Route Handlers to statically generate responses at build time for specified params, while handling other params dynamically at request time.\n\nWhen using [Cache Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/cache-components), you can combine &#96;generateStaticParams&#96; with &#96;use cache&#96; to enable data caching for both prerendered and runtime params.\n\nSee the [generateStaticParams with Route Handlers](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params#with-route-handlers) documentation for examples and details.\n\n### URL Query Parameters\n\nThe request object passed to the Route Handler is a &#96;NextRequest&#96; instance, which includes [some additional convenience methods](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request#nexturl), such as those for more easily handling query parameters.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { type NextRequest } from 'next/server'\n\nexport function GET(request: NextRequest) {\n  const searchParams = request.nextUrl.searchParams\n  const query = searchParams.get('query')\n  // query is \"hello\" for /api/search?query=hello\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport function GET(request) {\n  const searchParams = request.nextUrl.searchParams\n  const query = searchParams.get('query')\n  // query is \"hello\" for /api/search?query=hello\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Streaming\n\nStreaming is commonly used in combination with Large Language Models (LLMs), such as OpenAI, for AI-generated content. Learn more about the [AI SDK](https://sdk.vercel.ai/docs/introduction).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai'\nimport { StreamingTextResponse, streamText } from 'ai'\n\nexport async function POST(req: Request) {\n  const { messages } = await req.json()\n  const result = await streamText({\n    model: openai('gpt-4-turbo'),\n    messages,\n  })\n\n  return new StreamingTextResponse(result.toAIStream())\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai'\nimport { StreamingTextResponse, streamText } from 'ai'\n\nexport async function POST(req) {\n  const { messages } = await req.json()\n  const result = await streamText({\n    model: openai('gpt-4-turbo'),\n    messages,\n  })\n\n  return new StreamingTextResponse(result.toAIStream())\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThese abstractions use the Web APIs to create a stream. You can also use the underlying Web APIs directly.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\n// https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/ReadableStream#convert_async_iterator_to_stream\nfunction iteratorToStream(iterator: any) {\n  return new ReadableStream({\n    async pull(controller) {\n      const { value, done } = await iterator.next()\n\n      if (done) {\n        controller.close()\n      } else {\n        controller.enqueue(value)\n      }\n    },\n  })\n}\n\nfunction sleep(time: number) {\n  return new Promise((resolve) =\u003e {\n    setTimeout(resolve, time)\n  })\n}\n\nconst encoder = new TextEncoder()\n\nasync function* makeIterator() {\n  yield encoder.encode('\u003cp\u003eOne\u003c/p\u003e')\n  await sleep(200)\n  yield encoder.encode('\u003cp\u003eTwo\u003c/p\u003e')\n  await sleep(200)\n  yield encoder.encode('\u003cp\u003eThree\u003c/p\u003e')\n}\n\nexport async function GET() {\n  const iterator = makeIterator()\n  const stream = iteratorToStream(iterator)\n\n  return new Response(stream)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/ReadableStream#convert_async_iterator_to_stream\nfunction iteratorToStream(iterator) {\n  return new ReadableStream({\n    async pull(controller) {\n      const { value, done } = await iterator.next()\n\n      if (done) {\n        controller.close()\n      } else {\n        controller.enqueue(value)\n      }\n    },\n  })\n}\n\nfunction sleep(time) {\n  return new Promise((resolve) =\u003e {\n    setTimeout(resolve, time)\n  })\n}\n\nconst encoder = new TextEncoder()\n\nasync function* makeIterator() {\n  yield encoder.encode('\u003cp\u003eOne\u003c/p\u003e')\n  await sleep(200)\n  yield encoder.encode('\u003cp\u003eTwo\u003c/p\u003e')\n  await sleep(200)\n  yield encoder.encode('\u003cp\u003eThree\u003c/p\u003e')\n}\n\nexport async function GET() {\n  const iterator = makeIterator()\n  const stream = iteratorToStream(iterator)\n\n  return new Response(stream)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Request Body\n\nYou can read the &#96;Request&#96; body using the standard Web API methods:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\n  const res = await request.json()\n  return Response.json({ res })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function POST(request) {\n  const res = await request.json()\n  return Response.json({ res })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Request Body FormData\n\nYou can read the &#96;FormData&#96; using the &#96;request.formData()&#96; function:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\n  const formData = await request.formData()\n  const name = formData.get('name')\n  const email = formData.get('email')\n  return Response.json({ name, email })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function POST(request) {\n  const formData = await request.formData()\n  const name = formData.get('name')\n  const email = formData.get('email')\n  return Response.json({ name, email })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSince &#96;formData&#96; data are all strings, you may want to use [&#96;zod-form-data&#96;](https://www.npmjs.com/zod-form-data) to validate the request and retrieve data in the format you prefer (e.g. &#96;number&#96;).\n\n### CORS\n\nYou can set CORS headers for a specific Route Handler using the standard Web API methods:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',\n      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS',\n      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Content-Type, Authorization',\n    },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET(request) {\n  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',\n      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS',\n      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Content-Type, Authorization',\n    },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e - To add CORS headers to multiple Route Handlers, you can use [Proxy](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#cors) or the [&#96;next.config.js&#96; file](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers#cors).\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n### Webhooks\n\nYou can use a Route Handler to receive webhooks from third-party services:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\n  try {\n    const text = await request.text()\n    // Process the webhook payload\n  } catch (error) {\n    return new Response(&#96;Webhook error: ${error.message}&#96;, {\n      status: 400,\n    })\n  }\n\n  return new Response('Success!', {\n    status: 200,\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function POST(request) {\n  try {\n    const text = await request.text()\n    // Process the webhook payload\n  } catch (error) {\n    return new Response(&#96;Webhook error: ${error.message}&#96;, {\n      status: 400,\n    })\n  }\n\n  return new Response('Success!', {\n    status: 200,\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNotably, unlike API Routes with the Pages Router, you do not need to use &#96;bodyParser&#96; to use any additional configuration.\n\n### Non-UI Responses\n\nYou can use Route Handlers to return non-UI content. Note that [&#96;sitemap.xml&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap#generating-a-sitemap-using-code-js-ts), [&#96;robots.txt&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots#generate-a-robots-file), [&#96;app icons&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#generate-icons-using-code-js-ts-tsx), and [open graph images](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image) all have built-in support.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport async function GET() {\n  return new Response(\n headers: {\n        'Content-Type': 'text/xml',\n      },\n    }\n  )\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function GET() {\n  return new Response(&#96;\u003c?xml version=\"1.0\" true\nexport const revalidate = false\nexport const fetchCache = 'auto'\nexport const runtime = 'nodejs'\nexport const preferredRegion = 'auto'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport const 'auto'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSee the [API reference](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config) for more details.\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | Changes   "markdown": "# Route Segment Config\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\n\u003e - &#96;generateStaticParams&#96; cannot be used inside a &#96;'use client'&#96; file.\n\u003e - Route Segment options only take effect in Server Component Pages, Layouts, or Route Handlers.\n\u003e - The options outlined on this page are disabled if the [&#96;cacheComponents&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag is on, and will eventually be deprecated in the future.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\nThe Route Segment options allows you to configure the behavior of a [Page](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [Layout](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) by directly exporting the following variables:\n\n| Option | Type | Default |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [&#96;dynamic&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#dynamic) | &#96;'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'&#96; | &#96;'auto'&#96; |\n| [&#96;dynamicParams&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#dynamicparams) | &#96;boolean&#96; | &#96;true&#96; |\n| [&#96;revalidate&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#revalidate) | &#96;false | 0 | number&#96; | &#96;false&#96; |\n| [&#96;fetchCache&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#fetchcache) | &#96;'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache' | 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'&#96; | &#96;'auto'&#96; |\n| [&#96;runtime&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#runtime) | &#96;'nodejs' | 'edge'&#96; | &#96;'nodejs'&#96; |\n| [&#96;preferredRegion&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#preferredregion) | &#96;'auto' | 'global' | 'home' | string | string[]&#96; | &#96;'auto'&#96; |\n| [&#96;maxDuration&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#maxduration) | &#96;number&#96; | Set by deployment platform |\n\n## Options\n\n### &#96;dynamic&#96;\n\nChange the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts\" switcher\nexport const dynamic = 'auto'\n// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const dynamic = 'auto'\n// 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e Good to know: The new model in the &#96;app&#96; directory favors granular caching control at the &#96;fetch&#96; request level over the binary all-or-nothing model of &#96;getServerSideProps&#96; and &#96;getStaticProps&#96; at the page-level in the &#96;pages&#96; directory. The &#96;dynamic&#96; option is a way to opt back in to the previous model as a convenience and provides a simpler migration path.\n\n- &#96;'force-static'&#96;: Force static rendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [&#96;cookies&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [&#96;headers()&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [&#96;useSearchParams()&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [&#96;revalidate&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config#revalidate), [&#96;revalidatePath&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [&#96;revalidateTag&#96;](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with &#96;force-static&#96;.\n- &#96;'error'&#96;: Force static rendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use [Dynamic APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:&#96;getStaticProps()&#96; in the &#96;pages&#96; directory. Setting the option of every &#96;fetch()&#96; request in a layout or page to &#96;{ cache: 'force-cache' }&#96;. Setting the segment config to &#96;fetchCache = 'only-cache'&#96;.\n- &#96;'force-dynamic'&#96;: Force [dynamic rendering](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to: Setting the option of every &#96;fetch()&#96; request in a layout or page to &#96;{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }&#96;. Setting the segment config to &#96;export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'&#96;\n- &#96;'auto'&#96; (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.\n\n\u003e - Instructions on [how to migrate](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration#step-6-migrating-data-fetching-methods) from &#96;getServerSideProps&#96; and &#96;getStaticProps&#96; to &#96;dynamic: 'force-dynamic'&#96; and &#96;dynamic: 'error'&#96; can be found in the [upgrade guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration#step-6-migrating-data-fetching-methods).\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n### &#96;dynamicParams&#96;\n\nControl what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with [generateStaticParams](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx\" switcher\nexport const dynamicParams = true // true | false\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const dynamicParams = true // true | false\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- &#96;false&#96;: Dynamic segments not included in &#96;generateStaticParams&#96; will return a 404.\n- &#96;true&#96; (default): Dynamic segments not included in &#96;generateStaticParams&#96; are generated on demand.\n\n\u003e - When &#96;dynamicParams = true&#96;, the segment uses [Streaming Server Rendering](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#streaming).\n\u003e - To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, you'll need to return an empty array in &#96;generateStaticParams&#96; or utilize &#96;export const dynamic = 'force-static'&#96;.\n\u003e - This option replaces the &#96;fallback: true | false | blocking&#96; option of &#96;getStaticPaths&#96; in the &#96;pages&#96; directory.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n### &#96;revalidate&#96;\n\nSet the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the &#96;revalidate&#96; value set by individual &#96;fetch&#96; requests.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts\" switcher\nexport const revalidate = false\n// false | 0 | number\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const revalidate = false\n// false | 0 | number\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- &#96;number&#96;: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to &#96;n&#96; seconds.\n- &#96;0&#96;: Ensure a layout or page is always [dynamically rendered](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) even if no Dynamic APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of &#96;fetch&#96; requests that do not set a &#96;cache&#96; option to &#96;'no-store'&#96; but leaves &#96;fetch&#96; requests that opt into &#96;'force-cache'&#96; or use a positive &#96;revalidate&#96; as is.\n- &#96;false&#96; (default): The default heuristic to cache any &#96;fetch&#96; requests that set their &#96;cache&#96; option to &#96;'force-cache'&#96; or are discovered before a [Dynamic API](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) is used. Semantically equivalent to &#96;revalidate: Infinity&#96; which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual &#96;fetch&#96; requests to use &#96;cache: 'no-store'&#96; or &#96;revalidate: 0&#96; to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set &#96;revalidate&#96; to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.\n\n\u003e - In Development, Pages are always rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.\n\u003e - The revalidate value is not available when using &#96;runtime = 'edge'&#96;.\n\u003e - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example &#96;revalidate = 600&#96; is valid, but &#96;revalidate = 60 * 10&#96; is not.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n#### Revalidation Frequency\n\n- Individual &#96;fetch&#96; requests can set a lower &#96;revalidate&#96; than the route's default &#96;revalidate&#96; to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.\n- The lowest &#96;revalidate&#96; across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.\n\n### &#96;fetchCache&#96;\n\nBy default, Next.js will cache any &#96;fetch()&#96; requests that are reachable before any [Dynamic APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) are used and will not cache &#96;fetch&#96; requests that are discovered after Dynamic APIs are used.\n\n&#96;fetchCache&#96; allows you to override the default &#96;cache&#96; option of all &#96;fetch&#96; requests in a layout or page.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts\" switcher\nexport const fetchCache = 'auto'\n// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'\n// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const fetchCache = 'auto'\n// 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'\n// 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- &#96;'force-no-store'&#96;: Ensure all &#96;fetch&#96; requests opt out of caching by setting the &#96;cache&#96; option of all &#96;fetch&#96; requests to &#96;'no-store'&#96;. This forces all &#96;fetch&#96; requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a &#96;'force-cache'&#96; option.\n- &#96;'only-no-store'&#96;: Ensure all &#96;fetch&#96; requests opt out of caching by changing the default to &#96;cache: 'no-store'&#96; if no option is provided and causing an error if any &#96;fetch&#96; requests use &#96;cache: 'force-cache'&#96;\n- &#96;'default-no-store'&#96;: Allow any &#96;cache&#96; option to be passed to &#96;fetch&#96; but if no option is provided then set the &#96;cache&#96; option to &#96;'no-store'&#96;. This means that even &#96;fetch&#96; requests before Dynamic APIs are considered dynamic.\n- &#96;'force-cache'&#96;: Ensure all &#96;fetch&#96; requests opt into caching by setting the &#96;cache&#96; option of all &#96;fetch&#96; requests to &#96;'force-cache'&#96;.\n- &#96;'only-cache'&#96;: Ensure all &#96;fetch&#96; requests opt into caching by changing the default to &#96;cache: 'force-cache'&#96; if no option is provided and causing an error if any &#96;fetch&#96; requests use &#96;cache: 'no-store'&#96;.\n- &#96;'default-cache'&#96;: Allow any &#96;cache&#96; option to be passed to &#96;fetch&#96; but if no option is provided then set the &#96;cache&#96; option to &#96;'force-cache'&#96;. This means that even &#96;fetch&#96; requests after Dynamic APIs are considered static.\n- &#96;'auto'&#96; (default): The default option to cache &#96;fetch&#96; requests before Dynamic APIs with the &#96;cache&#96; option they provide and not cache &#96;fetch&#96; requests after Dynamic APIs.\n\n#### Cross-route segment behavior\n\n- It is generally recommended to leave shared parent layouts as &#96;'auto'&#96; and customize the options where child segments diverge.\n- Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other. If both the &#96;'only-cache'&#96; and &#96;'force-cache'&#96; are provided, then &#96;'force-cache'&#96; wins. If both &#96;'only-no-store'&#96; and &#96;'force-no-store'&#96; are provided, then &#96;'force-no-store'&#96; wins. The force option changes the behavior across the route so a single segment with &#96;'force-*'&#96; would prevent any errors caused by &#96;'only-*'&#96;. The intention of the &#96;'only-*'&#96; and &#96;'force-*'&#96; options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means: A combination of &#96;'only-cache'&#96; and &#96;'only-no-store'&#96; in a single route is not allowed. A combination of &#96;'force-cache'&#96; and &#96;'force-no-store'&#96; in a single route is not allowed. A parent cannot provide &#96;'default-no-store'&#96; if a child provides &#96;'auto'&#96; or &#96;'*-cache'&#96; since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.\n\n### &#96;runtime&#96;\n\nWe recommend using the Node.js runtime for rendering your application. This option cannot be used in [Proxy](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).\n\n\u003e Good to know: Using &#96;runtime: 'edge'&#96; is not supported for Cache Components.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts\" switcher\nexport const runtime = 'nodejs'\n// 'nodejs' | 'edge'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const runtime = 'nodejs'\n// 'nodejs' | 'edge'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- &#96;'edge'&#96;\n- &#96;'nodejs'&#96; (default)\n\n### &#96;preferredRegion&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts\" switcher\nexport const preferredRegion = 'auto'\n// 'auto' | 'global' | 'home' | ['iad1', 'sfo1']\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const preferredRegion = 'auto'\n// 'auto' | 'global' | 'home' | ['iad1', 'sfo1']\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSupport for &#96;preferredRegion&#96;, and regions supported, is dependent on your deployment platform.\n\n\u003e - The root layout defaults to &#96;all&#96; regions.\n\u003e - If a &#96;preferredRegion&#96; is not specified, it will inherit the option of the nearest parent layout.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n### &#96;maxDuration&#96;\n\nBy default, Next.js does not limit the execution of server-side logic (rendering a page or handling an API).\nDeployment platforms can use &#96;maxDuration&#96; from the Next.js build output to add specific execution limits.\n\nNote: This setting requires Next.js &#96;13.4.10&#96; or higher.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\"layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts\" switcher\nexport const maxDuration = 5\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js filename=\"layout.js | page.js | route.js\" switcher\nexport const maxDuration = 5\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\u003e - If using [Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data), set the &#96;maxDuration&#96; at the page level to change the default timeout of all Server Actions used on the page.\n\u003e \n\u003e Good to know:\n\n### &#96;generateStaticParams&#96;\n\nThe &#96;generateStaticParams&#96; function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to define the list of route segment parameters that will be statically generated at build time instead of on-demand at request time.\n\nSee the [API reference](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) for more details.\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;v16.0.0&#96; | &#96;export const experimental_ppr = true&#96; removed. A [codemod](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-experimental_ppr-route-segment-config-from-app-router-pages-and-layouts) is available. |\n| &#96;v15.0.0-RC&#96; | &#96;export const runtime = \"experimental-edge\"&#96; deprecated. A [codemod](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#transform-app-router-route-segment-config-runtime-value-from-experimental-edge-to-edge) is available. |\n\n---\n\nFor an overview of all available documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt)",

}

  "markdown": "# instrumentation.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nThe &#96;instrumentation.js|ts&#96; file is used to integrate observability tools into your application, allowing you to track the performance and behavior, and to debug issues in production.\n\nTo use it, place the file in the root of your application or inside a [&#96;src&#96; folder](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/src-folder) if using one.\n\n## Exports\n\n### &#96;register&#96; (optional)\n\nThe file exports a &#96;register&#96; function that is called once when a new Next.js server instance is initiated, and must complete before the server is ready to handle requests. &#96;register&#96; can be an async function.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'\n\nexport function register() {\n  registerOTel('next-app')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { registerOTel } from '@vercel/otel'\n\nexport function register() {\n  registerOTel('next-app')\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### &#96;onRequestError&#96; (optional)\n\nYou can optionally export an &#96;onRequestError&#96; function to track server errors to any custom observability provider.\n\n- The &#96;error&#96; instance might not be the original error instance thrown, as it may be processed by React if encountered during Server Components rendering. If this happens, you can use &#96;digest&#96; property on an error to identify the actual error type.\n- If you're running any async tasks in &#96;onRequestError&#96;, make sure they're awaited. &#96;onRequestError&#96; will be triggered when the Next.js server captures the error.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { type Instrumentation } from 'next'\n\nexport const onRequestError: Instrumentation.onRequestError = async (\n  err,\n  request,\n  context\n) =\u003e {\n  await fetch('https://.../report-error', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      message: err.message,\n      request,\n      context,\n    }),\n    headers: {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n    },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport async function onRequestError(err, request, context) {\n  await fetch('https://.../report-error', {\n    method: 'POST',\n    body: JSON.stringify({\n      message: err.message,\n      request,\n      context,\n    }),\n    headers: {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/json',\n    },\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Parameters\n\nThe function accepts three parameters: &#96;error&#96;, &#96;request&#96;, and &#96;context&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nexport function onRequestError(\n  error: { digest: string } \u0026 Error,\n  request: {\n    path: string // resource path, e.g. /blog?name=foo\n    method: string // request method. e.g. GET, POST, etc\n    headers: { [key: string]: string | string[] }\n  },\n  context: {\n    routerKind: 'Pages Router' | 'App Router' // the router type\n    routePath: string // the route file path, e.g. /app/blog/[dynamic]\n    routeType: 'render' | 'route' | 'action' | 'proxy' // the context in which the error occurred\n    renderSource:\n      | 'react-server-components'\n      | 'react-server-components-payload'\n      | 'server-rendering'\n    revalidateReason: 'on-demand' | 'stale' | undefined // undefined is a normal request without revalidation\n    renderType: 'dynamic' | 'dynamic-resume' // 'dynamic-resume' for PPR\n  }\n): void | Promise\u003cvoid\u003e\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- &#96;context&#96;: The context in which the error occurred. This can be the type of router (App or Pages Router), and/or (Server Components (&#96;'render'&#96;), Route Handlers (&#96;'route'&#96;), Server Actions (&#96;'action'&#96;), or Proxy (&#96;'proxy'&#96;)).\n- &#96;request&#96;: Read-only request information associated with the error.\n- &#96;error&#96;: The caught error itself (type is always &#96;Error&#96;), and a &#96;digest&#96; property which is the unique ID of the error.\n\n### Specifying the runtime\n\nThe &#96;instrumentation.js&#96; file works in both the Node.js and Edge runtime, however, you can use &#96;process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME&#96; to target a specific runtime.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nexport function register() {\n  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') {\n    return require('./register.edge')\n  } else {\n    return require('./register.node')\n  }\n}\n\nexport function onRequestError() {\n  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') {\n    return require('./on-request-error.edge')\n  } else {\n    return require('./on-request-error.node')\n  }\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Version History\n\n| Version | Changes |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;v15.0.0&#96; | &#96;onRequestError&#96; introduced, &#96;instrumentation&#96; stable |\n| &#96;v14.0.4&#96; | Turbopack support for &#96;instrumentation&#96; |\n| &#96;v13.2.0&#96; | &#96;instrumentation&#96; introduced as an experimental feature |\n\n## Learn more about Instrumentation- [Instrumentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/instrumentation)\n\n- Learn how to use instrumentation to run code at server startup in your Next.js app\n\n---\n\nFor an overview of all available documentation, see [/docs/llms.txt](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt)",

}

{
  "markdown": "# instrumentation-client.js\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\nThe &#96;instrumentation-client.js|ts&#96; file allows you to add monitoring, analytics code, and other side-effects that run before your application becomes interactive. This is useful for setting up performance tracking, error monitoring, polyfills, or any other client-side observability tools.\n\nTo use it, place the file in the root of your application or inside a &#96;src&#96; folder.\n\n## Usage\n\nUnlike [server-side instrumentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/instrumentation), you do not need to export any specific functions. You can write your monitoring code directly in the file:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\n// Set up performance monitoring\nperformance.mark('app-init')\n\n// Initialize analytics\nconsole.log('Analytics initialized')\n\n// Set up error tracking\nwindow.addEventListener('error', (event) =\u003e {\n  // Send to your error tracking service\n  reportError(event.error)\n})\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\n// Set up performance monitoring\nperformance.mark('app-init')\n\n// Initialize analytics\nconsole.log('Analytics initialized')\n\n// Set up error tracking\nwindow.addEventListener('error', (event) =\u003e {\n  // Send to your error tracking service\n  reportError(event.error)\n})\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nError handling: Implement try-catch blocks around your instrumentation code to ensure robust monitoring. This prevents individual tracking failures from affecting other instrumentation features.\n\n## Router navigation tracking\n\nYou can export an &#96;onRouterTransitionStart&#96; function to receive notifications when navigation begins:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nperformance.mark('app-init')\n\nexport function onRouterTransitionStart(\n  url: string,\n  navigationType: 'push' | 'replace' | 'traverse'\n) {\n  console.log(&#96;Navigation started: ${navigationType} to ${url}&#96;)\n  performance.mark(&#96;nav-start-${Date.now()}&#96;)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nperformance.mark('app-init')\n\nexport function onRouterTransitionStart(url, navigationType) {\n  console.log(&#96;Navigation started: ${navigationType} to ${url}&#96;)\n  performance.mark(&#96;nav-start-${Date.now()}&#96;)\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe &#96;onRouterTransitionStart&#96; function receives two parameters:\n\n- &#96;navigationType: 'push' | 'replace' | 'traverse'&#96; - The type of navigation\n- &#96;url: string&#96; - The URL being navigated to\n\n## Performance considerations\n\nKeep instrumentation code lightweight.\n\nNext.js monitors initialization time in development and will log warnings if it takes longer than 16ms, which could impact smooth page loading.\n\n## Execution timing\n\nThe &#96;instrumentation-client.js&#96; file executes at a specific point in the application lifecycle:\n\n1. Before user interactions are possible\n2. Before React hydration begins\n3. After the HTML document is loaded\n\nThis timing makes it ideal for setting up error tracking, analytics, and performance monitoring that needs to capture early application lifecycle events.\n\n## Examples\n\n### Error tracking\n\nInitialize error tracking before React starts and add navigation breadcrumbs for better debugging context.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport Monitor from './lib/monitoring'\n\nMonitor.initialize()\n\nexport function onRouterTransitionStart(url: string) {\n  Monitor.pushEvent({\n    message: &#96;Navigation to ${url}&#96;,\n    category: 'navigation',\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport Monitor from './lib/monitoring'\n\nMonitor.initialize()\n\nexport function onRouterTransitionStart(url) {\n  Monitor.pushEvent({\n    message: behavior analysis.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nimport { analytics } from './lib/analytics'\n\nanalytics.init()\n\nexport function onRouterTransitionStart(url: string, navigationType: string) {\n  analytics.track('page_navigation', {\n    url,\n    type: navigationType,\n    timestamp: Date.now(),\n  })\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;js\nimport { analytics } from './lib/analytics'\n\nanalytics.init()\n\nexport function onRouterTransitionStart(url, navigationType) {\n  analytics.track('page_navigation', {\n    url,\n    type: navigationType,\n    timestamp: list.getEntries()) {\n      if (entry instanceof PerformanceNavigationTiming) {\n        console.log('Time to Interactive:', entry.loadEventEnd - startTime)\n      }\n    }\n
